pages.x: For centuries Korea's kings had honoured the emperors of China as their overlords. But Japan, which had rebuilt itself on Western lines since 1868, wanted Korea in its own sphere. In 1894 a peasant rising, the Donghak rebellion, broke out, and China and Japan both sent troops, then refused to leave.

On 23 July 1894 Japanese troops seized the royal palace in Seoul and set up a government friendly to Japan. Two days later a Japanese cruiser sank a British steamer, the Kowshing, carrying Chinese troops to Korea, and hundreds of soldiers drowned. On 1 August the two empires declared war.

On 15 September the Japanese took Pyongyang and drove the Chinese out of Korea. Two days later, off the mouth of the Yalu River, Japan's fast new cruisers beat China's Beiyang Fleet, which hid in harbour for the rest of the war. It was said that navy money had been spent rebuilding the Empress Dowager's Summer Palace.

In November the Japanese stormed the fortress of Port Arthur, at the tip of the Liaodong peninsula. Enraged at finding the mutilated bodies of captured comrades, Japanese troops then killed many of the people of the town, soldiers and civilians alike. The reports of Western journalists shocked the world.
pages.of: killed in the town after it fell

pages.x: In January 1895 the Japanese landed in Shandong and took the forts of Weihaiwei from behind, trapping what was left of the Beiyang Fleet in its harbour. Torpedo boats slipped in at night and sank its ships. Admiral Ding Ruchang took his own life, and his officers surrendered the fleet.

China sent its senior statesman, Li Hongzhang, to make peace. At Shimonoseki a Japanese gunman shot him in the face, and the shame of it made Japan soften its terms. On 17 April 1895 he signed: China recognised Korea's independence, gave Japan Taiwan and the Liaodong peninsula, and paid a vast indemnity.

Within a week Russia, France and Germany made Japan give the Liaodong peninsula back, and three years later Russia leased its tip, Port Arthur, for itself. Japan, humiliated, built up its army and navy, and in 1904 went to war with Russia.

Japan's first colony was Taiwan. Its people declared a short-lived Republic of Formosa to resist, but Japanese troops crushed it within five months. Japan ruled the island for fifty years, until 1945.

The war showed that Japan had become a modern power, and that the Qing empire could no longer defend itself. The great powers scrambled for slices of China, Chinese reformers and revolutionaries began to demand change, and Korea, freed from China, fell into Japan's shadow, until Japan annexed it in 1910.
pts: A war between China and Japan over Korea
